% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch19_cld_examples.tex, lines 709--720.
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:wanner-curve-comparison}
Let \(K\) be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
\(C\) be a smooth proper algebraic curve, and let \(W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}\)
be open.  For a continuous function \(u:W\to\mathbf R\),
\[
                  \dprimeddprime[u]\geq0
        \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                  u\text{ is Thuillier-subharmonic}.
\]
Consequently every continuous CLD-psh function on \(W\) is
Thuillier-subharmonic.
\end{theorem}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part1/ch08_examples.tex, lines 2668--2687.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:ch08-annulus-skeleton}
Let $a\in K^\circ$ with $v(a)=\ell>0$ and let
\[
 A(\ell)=\{z\in\mathbf A^{1,\An}_K:0\leq v(z)\leq\ell\}
\]
be the corresponding closed annulus, the analytic generic fibre of
$\Spf R\{x,y\}/(xy-a)$ with $x=z$ and $y=a/z$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the map $s\mapsto\zeta_{0,\rme^{-s}}$ identifies $[0,\ell]$ with a
closed subset $\Gamma_{A}\subset A(\ell)$, and the retraction
$r(z)=\zeta_{0,|z|}$ is a continuous idempotent onto it;
\item for $f$ in the annulus algebra, $|f(z)|\leq|f(r(z))|$, and
$s\mapsto-\log|f(\zeta_{0,\rme^{-s}})|$ is concave and piecewise affine with
integral slopes;
\item $\Gamma_A$ carries the path metric of \cref{def:ch08-path-metric}, in
which it has length $\ell=v(a)$; in particular the edge length is the
valuation of the deformation parameter, and is independent of the model.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch15_poincare_lelong.tex, lines 317--329.
\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:ch15-log-smooth}
Let $f$ be an invertible analytic function on an open set $U\subset X$.  Then
$\log|f|$ is a smooth function on $U$ in the sense of
\Cref{chap:cld-forms}, and
\[
 \dprime\log|f|=-\dprime t,\qquad
 \ddprime\log|f|=-\ddprime t,\qquad
 \dprimeddprime\log|f|=0 ,
\]
where $t$ is the affine coordinate on $\mathbf R$ pulled back by the moment
map $f$, that is, $t=-\log|f|$.
\end{lemma}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch18_delta_forms.tex, lines 5080--5107.
\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p062-open-polyannulus-products-over-curves}
Let \(K\), \(C\), and \(W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}\) be as in
\Cref{thm:wanner-curve-comparison}.  Let \(s\geq0\), and for
\(1\leq i\leq s\) put
\[
 A_i=A^-_{r_i,R_i}
 =\{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
                  r_i<|T_i(z)|<R_i\},
 \qquad 0<r_i<R_i,\quad r_i,R_i\in|K^\times|.
\]
Write
\[
 X_s=W\times_K\prod_{i=1}^sA_i,
 \qquad p:X_s\longrightarrow W,
 \qquad q_i:X_s\longrightarrow A_i.
\]
If \(h\in C^0(X_s,\mathbf R)\) satisfies
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0\), then there are unique continuous functions
\(b,a_1,\ldots,a_s:W\to\mathbf R\) such that
\[
 h=p^*b+\sum_{i=1}^s(a_i\circ p)q_i^*\log|T_i|.
\tag{\(\heartsuit\)}\label{eq:p062-open-polyannulus-curve-formula}
\]
Here \(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0\), every \(a_i\) is locally constant,
and \(h\) is classically pluriharmonic.  In fact it is locally
\(\mathbf R\)-PL and Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.
\end{theorem}

% Book-local P06.2 integral annular coefficient monodromy, 20 September 2026.
\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p062-open-annulus-unit-integral-slope}
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed complete non-Archimedean field with
nontrivial absolute value, let $0<r<R$ belong to $|F^\times|$, and put
\[
 A=\{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,F})^{\mathrm{an}}:r<|T(z)|<R\}.
\]
For every $f\in\mathcal O(A)^\times$ there are unique
$\kappa\in\mathbf R$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-open-annulus-unit-integral-slope}
                 \log|f|=\kappa+n\log|T|
                 \quad\text{on }A.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-polyannulus-bundle-slope-local-system}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$C$ be a smooth proper algebraic curve, and let $W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$
be open.  Let $s\geq1$, and let $\pi:Y\to W$ be a morphism, where $Y$ is a
good, topologically separated, pure $(s+1)$-dimensional strict $K$-analytic
space.  Suppose that $W$ has an analytic open cover
$(U_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ for which, for radii
\[
 0<r_{\alpha,i}<R_{\alpha,i},
 \qquad r_{\alpha,i},R_{\alpha,i}\in|K^\times|
 \quad(1\leq i\leq s),
\]
there is an isomorphism over $U_\alpha$
\[
 \pi^{-1}(U_\alpha)\simeq
 U_\alpha\times_K\prod_{i=1}^s
 \{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
            r_{\alpha,i}<|T_{\alpha,i}(z)|<R_{\alpha,i}\}.
\]
Put
\[
 L_\alpha=
 \begin{pmatrix}
  \log|T_{\alpha,1}|\\[-2pt]
  \vdots\\[-2pt]
  \log|T_{\alpha,s}|
 \end{pmatrix}
 \quad\text{on }\pi^{-1}(U_\alpha).
\]
On every nonempty overlap $U_{\alpha\beta}=U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$ there
are unique maps
\[
 M_{\alpha\beta}:U_{\alpha\beta}\longrightarrow
      \operatorname{GL}_s(\mathbf Z),
 \qquad
 c_{\alpha\beta}:U_{\alpha\beta}\longrightarrow\mathbf R^s
\]
such that $M_{\alpha\beta}$ is locally constant, every component of
$c_{\alpha\beta}$ is continuous with zero $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''$-current,
and
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-annular-coordinate-transition}
 L_\beta
 =\pi^*c_{\alpha\beta}+
   (M_{\alpha\beta}\circ\pi)L_\alpha
 \quad\text{on }\pi^{-1}(U_{\alpha\beta}).
\end{equation}
On every triple overlap they satisfy
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-annular-affine-cocycle}
 M_{\alpha\gamma}=M_{\beta\gamma}M_{\alpha\beta},
 \qquad
 c_{\alpha\gamma}
 =c_{\beta\gamma}+M_{\beta\gamma}c_{\alpha\beta}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, the matrices define a rank-$s$ local system of lattices
$\mathbb{V}_{\pi,\mathbf Z}$ on $W$, well defined up to canonical
isomorphism under refinement or replacement of the trivializing atlas.
After putting
\[
 \mathbb{V}_{\pi,\mathbf R}
 =\mathbb{V}_{\pi,\mathbf Z}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R,
\]
the pairs $(M_{\alpha\beta},c_{\alpha\beta})$ define an affine
$\mathbb{V}_{\pi,\mathbf R}$-cocycle whose translation terms are
zero-current functions.

If $h\in C^0(Y,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$, its unique chartwise expressions are
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-annular-local-normal-form}
 h=\pi^*b_\alpha+
   (a_\alpha\circ\pi)^{\mathsf T}L_\alpha,
 \qquad
 \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b_\alpha]=0,
\end{equation}
where $a_\alpha:U_\alpha\to\mathbf R^s$ is locally constant.  On overlaps,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-annular-coefficient-transition}
 a_\alpha=M_{\alpha\beta}^{\mathsf T}a_\beta,
 \qquad
 b_\alpha=b_\beta+a_\beta^{\mathsf T}c_{\alpha\beta}.
\end{equation}
Thus the slope vectors define a global locally constant section of
$\mathbb{V}_{\pi,\mathbf R}^\vee$.  The failure of the chartwise logarithmic
coefficient data to glue in the chosen coordinates is recorded by the
integral linear monodromy $M_{\alpha\beta}$ and the zero-current translation
cocycle $c_{\alpha\beta}$; no choice of compatible global annular coordinates
is asserted.
\end{proposition}

% Book-local P06.2 zero-current radiance obstruction, 20 September 2026.
\begin{definition}
\label{def:p062-zero-current-radiance-class}
In the setting of
\Cref{prop:p062-polyannulus-bundle-slope-local-system}, let
$\mathscr P_W$ be the sheaf
\[
 \mathscr P_W(U)=
 \{b\in C^0(U,\mathbf R):\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0\}.
\]
Write $\mathscr P_W(\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R})$ for its twist by the real
local system $\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}$: in the frame indexed by $\alpha$,
a section is a vector of functions in $\mathscr P_W$, and its coordinates
transform by $d_\beta=M_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha$.

The translation vectors $c_{\alpha\beta}$ define a Cech class
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-zero-current-radiance-class}
 \rho_0(\pi)=[(c_{\alpha\beta})]
 \in
 \check H^1\bigl(W,\mathscr P_W(\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R})\bigr),
\end{equation}
where the right-hand side is the direct limit over refinements of analytic
open covers.  We call $\rho_0(\pi)$ the zero-current radiance class of the
polyannulus bundle.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-polyannulus-radiance-obstruction}
The class $\rho_0(\pi)$ is independent of the chosen trivializing atlas and
annular coordinates under the canonical identification of the resulting
local systems.  It vanishes if and only if, after possibly refining the
atlas, there are vectors
\[
 d_\alpha\in\mathscr P_W(U_\alpha)^s
\]
for which the zero-current affine gauges
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-radiance-gauged-logarithms}
 \widetilde L_\alpha=L_\alpha+\pi^*d_\alpha
\end{equation}
satisfy the purely linear transition law
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-radiance-linear-transition}
 \widetilde L_\beta
 =(M_{\alpha\beta}\circ\pi)\widetilde L_\alpha.
\end{equation}
Let $\mathscr C_Y^0$ denote the sheaf of continuous real-valued functions on
$Y$.  When these equivalent conditions hold, the $\widetilde L_\alpha$ glue
to a global continuous section
\[
 \Lambda_\pi\in H^0(Y,\mathcal E_\pi),
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_\pi
 =\mathscr C_Y^0\otimes_{\mathbf R}\pi^{-1}\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R},
\]
of the flat real vector bundle associated with the pulled-back local system.

For any such choice of gauges and every $h\in C^0(Y,\mathbf R)$ with
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$, let
$a\in H^0(W,\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}^\vee)$ be the parallel dual section
given by \Cref{prop:p062-polyannulus-bundle-slope-local-system}.  Then there
is a unique $b\in\mathscr P_W(W)$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-radiance-global-coefficient-formula}
 h=\pi^*b+\langle\pi^{-1}a,\Lambda_\pi\rangle.
\end{equation}
In particular, vanishing of
$\check H^1(W,\mathscr P_W(\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}))$ removes the entire
zero-current translation obstruction.  This conclusion concerns affine
gauges of logarithmic absolute values; it does not assert that the
$d_\alpha$ are logarithms of analytic units or that the bundle admits global
annular coordinates.
\end{proposition}
proof:
\begin{proof}
Since $F$ is algebraically closed and nontrivially valued, $|F^\times|$ is
dense in $\mathbf R_{>0}$.  Let
\[
 A' = \{r'\leq|T|\leq R'\},
 \qquad r<r'<R'<R,
 \qquad r',R'\in|F^\times|,
\]
be a strict closed subannulus of $A$.  Both $f|_{A'}$ and its inverse belong
to the annulus algebra of $A'$.  After rescaling the coordinate,
\Cref{prop:ch08-annulus-skeleton} shows that
\[
 s\longmapsto-\log|f(\zeta_{0,\rme^{-s}})|
\]
is concave and piecewise affine with integral slopes on the skeleton of
$A'$.  Applying the same result to $f^{-1}$ shows that its negative is also
concave.  It is therefore affine, with an integral slope.

The maximum inequality in that proposition, first for $f$ and then for
$f^{-1}$, gives
\[
 |f(z)|\leq|f(r_{A'}(z))|,
 \qquad
 |f(z)|^{-1}\leq|f(r_{A'}(z))|^{-1}.
\]
Hence equality holds in both inequalities, so the integral affine formula
on the skeleton gives
\eqref{eq:p062-open-annulus-unit-integral-slope} on all of $A'$.  Such
closed strict subannuli cover $A$, and any two are contained in a third one.
Uniqueness of an affine function on a nondegenerate interval makes their
constants and integral slopes agree.  This proves the lemma.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Fix $\alpha$ and $\beta$.  Every $T_{\beta,k}$ is an invertible analytic
function on $\pi^{-1}(U_{\alpha\beta})$, so
\Cref{lem:ch15-log-smooth} gives
\[
 \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[\log|T_{\beta,k}|]=0.
\]
Use the $\alpha$-trivialization and apply
\Cref{thm:p062-open-polyannulus-products-over-curves} to this function.
Its unique coefficient formula gives a continuous zero-current function
$c_{\alpha\beta,k}$ on $U_{\alpha\beta}$ and locally constant real-valued
functions $M_{\alpha\beta,ki}$ such that
\[
 \log|T_{\beta,k}|
 =\pi^*c_{\alpha\beta,k}
  +\sum_{i=1}^s(M_{\alpha\beta,ki}\circ\pi)
                      \log|T_{\alpha,i}|.
\]
Collecting the $s$ identities gives
\eqref{eq:p062-annular-coordinate-transition}, initially with
$M_{\alpha\beta}$ valued in $\operatorname{Mat}_{s\times s}(\mathbf R)$.

We next prove that every entry is integral.  Fix
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and a complete algebraically closed extension
 $F/\mathscr H(x)$.  For a fixed $i$, choose $F$-points in all the annular
factors except the $i$-th one; such points exist because $|F^\times|$ is
dense.  Pullback preserves invertibility, so restricting the base change of
$T_{\beta,k}$ to the resulting one-dimensional open annulus gives an
analytic unit $f_{x,i}$.  The coefficient identity is preserved by base
change and restricts to
\[
 \log|f_{x,i}|=\kappa_{x,i}
       +M_{\alpha\beta,ki}(x)\log|T_{\alpha,i}|
\]
for a real constant $\kappa_{x,i}$.  The lemma and uniqueness of the slope
give $M_{\alpha\beta,ki}(x)\in\mathbf Z$.  This holds for every $x$, $i$,
and $k$, so $M_{\alpha\beta}$ is integer-valued.

Apply the same construction with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ reversed and
substitute the two formulas.  The resulting expression of $L_\alpha$ in
the $\alpha$-coordinates has linear coefficient
$M_{\beta\alpha}M_{\alpha\beta}$.  Uniqueness in the cited product theorem,
applied componentwise, compares it with the tautological expression
$L_\alpha=0+I_sL_\alpha$ and gives
\[
 M_{\beta\alpha}M_{\alpha\beta}=I_s,
 \qquad
 c_{\beta\alpha}+M_{\beta\alpha}c_{\alpha\beta}=0.
\]
Both matrices are integer-valued, so every $M_{\alpha\beta}$ lies in
$\operatorname{GL}_s(\mathbf Z)$.  On a triple overlap, substitute the
$\alpha$-to-$\beta$ formula into the $\beta$-to-$\gamma$ formula and compare
with the direct $\alpha$-to-$\gamma$ formula.  The same uniqueness gives
exactly \eqref{eq:p062-annular-affine-cocycle}.

The first identity in \eqref{eq:p062-annular-affine-cocycle} is the
transition law for a local system of lattices.  If the trivializing atlas is
replaced, apply the same construction to the union of the two atlases.  The
integral overlap matrices give an isomorphism between the two resulting
local systems, and uniqueness makes these isomorphisms compatible on triple
overlaps.  This proves the asserted independence up to canonical
isomorphism.  The second identity is the affine cocycle law for the
translation terms after realification.

Now let $h$ have zero current.  Applying the product theorem in each chart
gives the unique expression \eqref{eq:p062-annular-local-normal-form}.
Substitute \eqref{eq:p062-annular-coordinate-transition} into the
$\beta$-expression and compare it with the $\alpha$-expression.  Uniqueness
of the base and slope coefficients gives
\eqref{eq:p062-annular-coefficient-transition}.  The first of those
identities is precisely the dual real transition law, so the $a_\alpha$
define a global locally constant section of
$\mathbb{V}_{\pi,\mathbf R}^\vee$.  The second identity records the remaining
affine translation and completes the proof.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
The affine cocycle identity in
\eqref{eq:p062-annular-affine-cocycle} reads
\[
 c_{\alpha\gamma}
 =c_{\beta\gamma}+M_{\beta\gamma}c_{\alpha\beta}.
\]
This is exactly the Cech one-cocycle law for
$\mathscr P_W(\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R})$, with
$c_{\alpha\beta}$ written in the $\beta$-frame.  The sheaf is well defined
because its transition matrices are locally constant: multiplying a vector
of zero-current functions by such a matrix again gives a vector of
zero-current functions.  The reverse-transition identity from the same
proposition gives
$c_{\beta\alpha}=-M_{\beta\alpha}c_{\alpha\beta}$, while the identity chart
has zero translation, so this cocycle has the required alternating
normalization.

We first check independence.  On a common refinement, let
$\widehat L_\alpha$ be the logarithmic vector associated with a second set
of annular coordinates.  Applying
\Cref{prop:p062-polyannulus-bundle-slope-local-system} to the old and new
charts on the same open set gives
\[
 \widehat L_\alpha=\pi^*e_\alpha+(N_\alpha\circ\pi)L_\alpha,
 \qquad
 N_\alpha\in\operatorname{GL}_s(\mathbf Z),
 \qquad
 e_\alpha\in\mathscr P_W(U_\alpha)^s,
\]
with $N_\alpha$ locally constant.  Substitution in the two overlap formulas
gives
\[
 \widehat M_{\alpha\beta}
 =N_\beta M_{\alpha\beta}N_\alpha^{-1},
 \qquad
 \widehat c_{\alpha\beta}
 =N_\beta c_{\alpha\beta}
   +e_\beta-\widehat M_{\alpha\beta}e_\alpha.
\]
The first identity is the canonical change of frame for the local system;
under it, the second changes the translated cocycle by the Cech coboundary
of $(e_\alpha)$.  Thus the class is unchanged.  Passing to the union of two
atlases and then to a common refinement proves independence under
replacement of the atlas as well.

For a zero-cochain $d=(d_\alpha)$, formula
\eqref{eq:p062-annular-coordinate-transition} gives
\[
 \widetilde L_\beta
 =\pi^*\bigl(c_{\alpha\beta}+d_\beta
                 -M_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha\bigr)
  +(M_{\alpha\beta}\circ\pi)\widetilde L_\alpha.
\]
Hence \eqref{eq:p062-radiance-linear-transition} holds precisely when
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-radiance-coboundary}
 c_{\alpha\beta}+d_\beta-M_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha=0.
\end{equation}
By the direct-limit definition of Cech cohomology, such a zero-cochain
exists after a refinement precisely when $\rho_0(\pi)=0$.  The purely
linear transition law then glues the local continuous vectors
$\widetilde L_\alpha$ to the asserted section $\Lambda_\pi$ of
$\mathcal E_\pi$.  They are not claimed to be locally constant along the
fibres.

Let $h$ have zero current.  In the notation of
\eqref{eq:p062-annular-local-normal-form}, put
\[
 \widetilde b_\alpha=b_\alpha-a_\alpha^{\mathsf T}d_\alpha.
\]
The function $\widetilde b_\alpha$ has zero current because $a_\alpha$ is
locally constant.  On an overlap, use
\eqref{eq:p062-annular-coefficient-transition} and
\eqref{eq:p062-radiance-coboundary} to obtain
\begin{align*}
 \widetilde b_\alpha
 &=b_\beta+a_\beta^{\mathsf T}c_{\alpha\beta}
   -a_\beta^{\mathsf T}M_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha\\
 &=b_\beta-a_\beta^{\mathsf T}d_\beta
 =\widetilde b_\beta.
\end{align*}
Thus the $\widetilde b_\alpha$ glue to
$b\in\mathscr P_W(W)$.  Since
$a_\alpha=M_{\alpha\beta}^{\mathsf T}a_\beta$ and
$\widetilde L_\beta=M_{\alpha\beta}\widetilde L_\alpha$, their pairing is
independent of the chart.  Rewriting the original local formula as
\[
 h=\pi^*\widetilde b_\alpha
   +(a_\alpha\circ\pi)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde L_\alpha
\]
therefore gives \eqref{eq:p062-radiance-global-coefficient-formula}.
Uniqueness follows from the uniqueness of the chartwise base coefficient in
\Cref{prop:p062-polyannulus-bundle-slope-local-system}.  The cohomological
vanishing assertion is immediate from
\eqref{eq:p062-zero-current-radiance-class}, and the final qualification
records that the correcting zero-cochain was chosen in $\mathscr P_W$, not
in the sheaf of logarithms of analytic units.
\end{proof}
